The current code passes all tests (as the spec states — this is a refactoring exercise, not a bug fix). The repo has no commits; all files are untracked. Now I'll rewrite `markdown.go` as a clean, line-oriented parser.

I've verified the design against all 17 test cases:
- **Emphasis/strong**: the original applies one pair of `__…__` and one pair of `_…_` to the whole document up front — I'll preserve that exact behavior in a small helper.
- **Headers**: 1–6 leading `#` followed by a space → `<hN>`; 7+ hashes (the "h7" case) fall through to a paragraph, and `#`/`*` appearing mid-line are never interpreted (only line prefixes are checked).
- **Lists**: leading `* ` opens/continues a `<ul>`; the list is closed when a non-list line (header or paragraph) appears or at end of input.

All 17 tests pass, and `gofmt`/`go vet` are clean. ## What I did The spec (`.docs/instructions.md`) is a refactoring exercise: the original `markdown.go` worked but was a single character-scanning loop tangled with global flags (`header`, `list`, `listOpened`, `he`) and bizarre special cases (e.g. "header level 7" handled via `fmt.Sprintf` with `strings.Repeat`). I rewrote it in `markdown.go` as a line-oriented parser: 1. **`applyEmphasis`** — converts the first `__…__` pair to `` and first `_…_` pair to `` over the whole document, exactly preserving the original up-front replacement behavior. 2. **Line loop in `Render`** — each line is dispatched to exactly one of three cases: - **Header** (`headerLevel`): 1–6 leading `#` followed by a space → `…`; 7+ hashes (the "h7" case) and mid-line `#`/`*` are never interpreted, so they fall through to paragraph text. - **List item**: leading `* ` opens `
    ` on first use, appends `
  • `, and `closeList` emits `
` when a non-list line or end-of-input follows. - **Paragraph**: everything else → `

…

`. 3. **`closeList`** helper centralizes list termination, replacing the original's scattered `listOpened` flag juggling. Refactoring notes are recorded in comments as the spec suggested. No new files were created, and `markdown_test.go`/`cases_test.go` are untouched. `. That's untested either way, but strictly an improvement.
